name: The Benjamin Royal Sonesta
positioning: The Benjamin Royal Sonesta New York: a 1927 Emery Roth building on Lexington Avenue in Midtown East, renovated in 2024, with a signature sleep program
best_for: Travelers who want a Midtown East base one block from Grand Central Terminal
Families and longer stays who want rooms with kitchenettes
Guests who care about sleep and want a dedicated sleep program

facts.text: The hotel is on Lexington Avenue in Midtown East, one block from Grand Central Terminal.
Architect Emery Roth completed the hotel's 26-story Lexington Avenue building in 1927, designed to feel more like a Manhattan residence than a commercial tower.
The Neo-Romanesque building is one of the most recognized works of architect Emery Roth.
The building became an official New York City landmark in 2017.
In 2024 the hotel completed a full renovation of the lobby and all guestrooms and suites with design firm DLR Group.
Because the building was originally designed as apartments, the guest rooms are larger than standard Manhattan hotel rooms.
Guest Rooms feature herringbone wood floors, custom work desks and a kitchenette.
Rest & Renew sleep amenities include a meditation cushion, a Loftie alarm clock and night light, a Nodpod weighted blanket and on-demand meditations.
Every room comes with a curated physical book through the hotel's partnership with Bedside Reading.
The Kids Sleep Program was developed with sleep expert Dr. Rebecca Robbins.
The hotel's mascot, Oscar, The King of New York, is drawn from the original building facade.
At the on-site restaurant, The Parliament, Chef Rakmin Lee cooks modern American food with Korean, French and Italian threads.

highlights.text: Georgia O'Keeffe captured the building's silhouette in her painting New York Night.
Terrace Suites have private furnished terraces that overlook the city, with a separate bedroom, living area and kitchenette.
The Beverly Penthouse has a private outdoor corner terrace with views of the Manhattan skyline.
The Rest & Renew sleep program is the hotel's signature in-room wellness experience.
The 2024 renovation drew on two design inspirations: Benjamin, in bold architectural details, and Beverly, the building's original 1927 name, in softer gilded curves.

considerations.text: Some rooms face an active city street; guests who prefer a quieter room are encouraged to request an interior-facing room or a higher floor when booking.
A Hotel Facilities Fee is charged per room, per night.
Guests must be 21 or older to check in.
